messages:
julia: Planning a migration tonight during the 01:00-02:00 UTC change window. It adds `counter_v2` and a backfill that updates ~120M rows, done in small batches with advisory locks. Will coordinate deploy and DB job.

mike_dba: Thanks — what's the backfill strategy? are we using partitioned batch keys?

julia: We'll iterate by `shard_id` (0..63), each shard ~2M rows. Backfill job uses `LIMIT 1000` per transaction and sleeps between shards. Pseudocode: 
```sql
UPDATE metrics SET counter_v2 = counter_v1 WHERE shard_id = $shard AND counter_v2 IS NULL LIMIT 1000;
```
We also take `pg_advisory_lock(hashtext('backfill:shard:'||shard))` per shard to avoid overlap.

sam_p: Will the app read from both columns during rollout? Need feature-flag and a pinned model version for the next 24h.

julia: Yes — feature flag `use_counter_v2` gated per release. We'll deploy schema + code together in the canary, then enable the flag. If anything goes wrong we roll back flag then code.

anna_qe: Can we get a quick smoke checklist? I'll run a small subset locally.

mike_dba: DB notes: run plan in read-replica first to estimate time. Also moving this to lower concurrency if replication lag spikes. I recommend setting `pg_stat_replication` threshold at 10s.

sam_p: Deploy bot: queueing release 2026.03.20-rc3 for julia/migration.
deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.20-rc3 queued on cluster-prod-1. Hooks: predeploy db-check, migrate-job:scheduled.

oncall_bot: Reminder: change window is 01:00-02:00 UTC. Pager escalation enabled from 01:00 to 03:00 for possible fallout.

julia: Timeline: 00:45 - prechecks, 01:00 - deploy canary to 5% (no routing to canary DB jobs), 01:10 - start shard 0-7 backfills (staggered), 01:30 - evaluate, 01:40 - roll additional shards in waves if no issues, 01:50 - enable flag, 01:55 - monitor, 02:00 - end window and notice.

mike_dba: Emergency rollback plan: kill backfill jobs (we track by job-id), flip `use_counter_v2=false`, deploy previous app image tag pinned in the release notes -> `app:image@sha256:abc123` . Backfills are idempotent so partial progress is fine.

anna_qe: I'll add quick assertions: counts of null `counter_v2`, sample consistency checks `SELECT id FROM metrics WHERE counter_v2 IS NULL LIMIT 10;` and compare top 100 hot shards.

sam_p: Also pin the migration worker to `worker:1.4.2` for tonight; we've seen a threading bug in 1.4.3. Add this to release notes.

julia: Added to release notes: "Pin migration worker to worker:1.4.2. Backfill uses advisory locks per shard, batch size 1000, sleep 200ms between txns. Rollback: flip flag + stop jobs."

deploy-bot: Predeploy checks passed. Canary deploy started for 5% traffic.
julia: Canary healthy so far, starting shard 0-3.
mike_dba: Replication lag 2s -> OK.

another short pause...

anna_qe: Found one case where `counter_v1` was NULL but `counter_v2` expected non-null. Adding a defensive coalesce in job. Patch pushed.
sam_p: Rebuilding canary with patched worker, redeploy queued.

deploy-bot: Canary redeploy completed. Starting backfill shard 4-7.

julia: Monitoring metrics: CPU and IO within expected. Backfill throughput ~900 rows/s per worker.
mike_dba: Good. Continue but if lag >10s we throttle to 250 rows/s.

oncall_bot: 01:28 UTC - alert: minor spike in DB read latency (p95 from 60ms -> 320ms). Tagged severity: low.

julia: Throttling backfills to reduce concurrency, pausing shards 12-15 wave.
sam_p: Noted. Will keep worker pool at current size.

mike_dba: After wave completes, run final verification scripts and then enable `use_counter_v2` flag for 100% traffic.

julia: If all checks pass we'll flip flag at ~01:52 and run smoke tests.

deploy-bot: Release 2026.03.20-rc3 completed. Canary -> prod rollout continuing per plan.

julia: FLIP: `use_counter_v2=true` -> smoke tests green. Monitoring 10m.

anna_qe: Smoke OK on 10m. Sampling 200 rows, all consistent. :thumbsup:

mike_dba: Post-mortem note for changelog: consider smaller batch size for shard 0 (hot shard). Also add histogram to dashboard for future runs.

julia: Thanks team — closing thread. Will open follow-up doc with runbook and job ids.
